title: Implantable human-scale organs assembled outside the body

concept.text: The innovation is a clinically sized organ assembled outside the body, then implanted to replace the essential work of a failed organ for a durable period. Assembly could involve growing organized tissue or repopulating a decellularized organ scaffold with functional cells. A successful kidney construct would provide sufficient renal function to free a recipient from dialysis, with blood vessels and a urinary outlet integrated into the recipient. The supplied kidney study develops one route toward this goal using a porcine scaffold repopulated with human cells.

Conceptual synthesis. The intended capability combines organ construction, physiological integration, durable clinical function and reproducible manufacture. Human scale includes both clinically useful size and sufficient functional capacity. Success would be established separately for each organ, because a kidney, heart, liver or lung requires its own cellular organization, physiological functions and connections to the recipient.

significance.text: The supplied study motivates bioengineered kidney grafts through chronic shortages of donated kidneys. If manufactured grafts could durably replace essential organ function, they could substantially reduce dependence on human donors and expand access to transplantation. For a successful kidney platform, a direct clinical consequence would be sustained freedom from dialysis among recipients whose grafts provide adequate renal function.

Conditional synthesis. On-demand replacement would additionally require adequate production capacity, predictable manufacturing times, quality control, distribution and recipient compatibility. Several years of successful graft function would establish one important part of that capability. Reliable availability would require its own demonstration. A platform using decellularized porcine scaffolds would retain an animal-tissue sourcing dependency, even as it reduced dependence on donated human organs.

The potential impact also depends on immune management and organ-appropriate integration. Allogeneic cells require an effective strategy for controlling immune rejection. Freedom from immunosuppression would be an additional achievement, while clinically useful replacement could employ immunosuppression. The kidney study itself anticipates developing an immunosuppression protocol for future long-term testing. Requirements for innervation depend on the organ and the functions needed for clinical benefit.

Conditional synthesis. Demonstrating one manufactured organ could provide methods and experience relevant to others, including vascularization, cell production and graft quality assessment. Each additional organ would still require independent evidence of sufficient function, safety and durability. The supplied kidney experiment provides a limited basis for predicting clinical outcomes in other organs.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is an implantable, human-scale construct that performs the organ’s essential work durably enough to replace dialysis or a donor graft. The supplied 2024 kidney study establishes an early step through glomerular recellularization and acute filtration testing. Survival-supporting renal replacement, sustained dialysis independence and long-term function in a person remain beyond what that evidence demonstrates.

A central kidney-specific barrier is extending filtration-barrier activity into sufficiently complete renal function. The studied constructs contained endothelial cells and podocytes, while renal tubular epithelial cells were absent. Tubular functions governing fluid, electrolytes and solute handling therefore remain a major engineering gap. Cell maturity, the necessary diversity of cell types, their spatial organization and coordinated function must be established at clinically useful scale. The authors identify scale-up and multicell culture as continuing hurdles.

Durable vascular and urinary integration must also be demonstrated. A graft needs sustained blood perfusion, functional drainage and sufficient preservation of its cellular architecture over time. The study’s small acute implant series, changing surgical protocols and limited reproducibility leave substantial work in surgical integration, chronic graft performance and immune management.

Engineering synthesis. A clinically deployable platform would also need reproducible cell and scaffold inputs, consistent manufacturing yield, release tests that predict useful function, and a practical supply chain. Recipient compatibility and organ-dependent requirements such as innervation must be resolved according to the intended clinical use. The supplied evidence leaves the breadth and present-day status of these capabilities across the field unresolved.

current_state.text: Lo and colleagues’ study, published in Communications Medicine on 5 December 2024, reports decellularized porcine kidney scaffolds repopulated with human umbilical-vein endothelial cells and podocytes differentiated from human glomerular outgrowth cells. The authors describe recapitulation of glomerular structure, filtration during normothermic perfusion outside the body, and urine production after heterotopic implantation in pigs. These observations constitute an acute preclinical demonstration of aspects of kidney filtration.

The supplied review reports that five constructs were tested across three successive implant sessions, with surgical protocols changing between sessions. The first session failed to demonstrate filtration. The final session tested one construct over an observation window of up to five hours. The authors characterize the in vivo findings as preliminary and acknowledge limited sample size and reproducibility. These details materially constrain the demonstrated duration and consistency of function.

Functional assessment focused principally on protein and red-blood-cell exclusion, alongside urine-flow, protein and hematocrit measurements. A clinically interpretable physiological clearance measurement is unestablished in the supplied account. Renal tubular epithelial cells were omitted, and electrolyte and glucose readouts were omitted. Fluid and electrolyte regulation, complete kidney function, long-term graft performance and human replacement efficacy remain unestablished by these experiments. Urine production and filtration-barrier measurements alone leave the essential question of adequate renal replacement open.

The supplied review identifies the retained article as complete, with methods, results and discussion available, including the five-hour observation. This corrects the earlier research account’s assertion that truncation prevented extraction of implant duration. The review assessed narrative results and figure captions as supplied text. Figure images and supplementary datasets were unavailable for independent inspection. Several authors disclosed current or former employment at Miromatrix, a United Therapeutics subsidiary.

Evidence-scope synthesis. The BMC Nephrology item dated 11 February 2025 was retained only as a search lead, and the organoid literature encountered a publisher access barrier during the earlier research. Neither contributes inspected findings to this record. The supplied evidence therefore supports the dated 2024 kidney findings while leaving comparative leadership, later developments and clinical achievements in other externally assembled organs unresolved. The freshness record is empty, so the assessment does not establish the field’s status as of 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. A prospective human series would show that implanted constructs of at least one vital organ replace its essential function for several years, with clinically acceptable safety and durability. For kidney replacement, the proposed outcome is sustained freedom from dialysis, stable filtration and adequate regulation of fluid, electrolytes and other essential renal functions. Several years is a proposed threshold for this record. A clinical protocol would need to justify and specify the duration, sample size and functional endpoints.
completion_criteria.label: Implanted constructs replace essential organ function for several years

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical comparison. Evaluation would measure graft-threatening thrombosis, infection, rejection, graft loss and recipient outcomes against a clinically appropriate transplantation comparator, such as deceased-donor kidney transplantation. Comparisons would require adjustment for recipient and donor characteristics, together with prespecified safety margins and follow-up. The original aspiration of comparable complication rates requires these definitions before it can serve as a convincing test.
completion_criteria.label: Adjusted transplantation comparisons report complications against prespecified safety margins

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and supply demonstration. Outcomes would be reproduced across independently manufactured graft batches, multiple recipients and suitably independent clinical teams or sites. Documented manufacturing yield, release criteria, delivery times and treatment capacity would establish whether supply extends beyond exceptional or compassionate-use cases. Claims of on-demand availability would require explicit production and logistics targets in addition to clinical efficacy.
completion_criteria.label: Clinical outcomes reproduce independently with documented manufacturing supply capacity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries. Acute perfusion, hours-long animal implantation and external organ-assist systems would contribute intermediate evidence toward the implantable replacement goal. Completion would require durable implanted function in people. Reports should specify eligible recipients, immune-management requirements, organ-specific physiological integration and observed failure modes. A finite series would establish demonstrated performance within those conditions, with broader populations and additional organs requiring further validation.
completion_criteria.label: Durable human implanted function with reported clinical requirements and limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based conceptual synthesis. CLM-05, Durable organ xenotransplantation at clinical scale, overlaps in organ replacement, surgical integration, immune management and potential use of pigs. Its defining approach transplants a living animal organ. CLM-11 centers on assembling an organ outside the body, including through decellularization and recellularization. A porcine extracellular-matrix scaffold creates a material and sourcing overlap between the approaches while preserving their distinct construction methods.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. CLM-06, Therapeutic remuscularization of the adult human heart, shares the ambition of restoring organ-level function through functional tissue. Its focus is rebuilding muscle within an existing heart. CLM-11 concerns an externally assembled implantable organ and the additional demands of whole-graft construction and integration.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. CLM-15, Restoration of nephron number in the adult human kidney, overlaps directly with kidney cell biology and the need for functional nephron structures. It targets formation or restoration of nephrons within a native kidney. CLM-11 targets an externally assembled replacement graft, whose vascular supply, drainage and sufficient aggregate renal function must be established after implantation.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis. CLM-01, Programmable antigen-specific immune tolerance, could contribute to acceptance of allogeneic cells or other immunogenic graft components. Successful tolerance could reduce the burden of long-term immunosuppression. CLM-11 could also achieve clinically useful replacement with an effective conventional immune-management strategy, leaving immunosuppression-free transplantation as a further advance.

change_log.change: Preserved CLM-11’s identity and expanded the explanation of externally assembled, clinically sized replacement organs.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent despite limitations in the evidence supporting individual assertions.

change_log.change: Replaced the earlier truncation account with the review’s complete-text assessment and recovered implant duration.
change_log.reason: The retained article includes the results and reports a final observation window of up to five hours.

change_log.change: Added the five-construct, three-session design, changing surgical protocols, unsuccessful first-session filtration and single-construct final session.
change_log.reason: These details establish the limited sample size, duration and reproducibility of the reported preclinical result.

change_log.change: Distinguished filtration-barrier measurements and urine production from physiological clearance and sufficient renal replacement.
change_log.reason: Protein and red-blood-cell exclusion leave essential renal functions unestablished, particularly with tubular epithelial cells absent.

change_log.change: Qualified field-wide absence and comparative leadership claims, while preserving the documented 2024 achievement.
change_log.reason: One dated study and an empty freshness record cannot establish the strongest result or the field’s status in November 2026.

change_log.change: Separated durable replacement from on-demand availability and retained the porcine-scaffold sourcing dependency.
change_log.reason: Availability additionally depends on manufacturing capacity, quality control, logistics and recipient compatibility.

change_log.change: Recast freedom from immunosuppression as an additional ambition and made innervation requirements organ-dependent.
change_log.reason: Useful allogeneic replacement can employ immune suppression, and physiological integration requirements vary by organ.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include renal regulation, comparator adjustment, reproducibility and measurable supply capacity.
change_log.reason: The review identified these details as necessary to operationalize the proposed clinical demonstration. The thresholds remain proposals.

change_log.change: Preserved access limitations for the BMC search lead, organoid literature, figure images and supplementary datasets.
change_log.reason: Their evidentiary contribution must remain bounded by what the supplied review actually assessed.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with CLM-01, CLM-05, CLM-06 and CLM-15 as roster-based conceptual synthesis.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies identities and titles, while detailed evidence for those entries was unavailable.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record leaves developments after the December 2024 study and the field’s status as of 1 November 2026 unresolved.

A clinically interpretable physiological clearance measurement is unestablished in the supplied account. Exact urine-flow, protein and hematocrit values were not reproduced in the supplied review, so no additional numerical values are inferred.
Figure images and supplementary datasets were unavailable for independent inspection in the supplied review.
The BMC Nephrology search lead and access-limited organoid literature remain unassessed.
Durable complete renal replacement, long-term vascular and urinary integration, immune management and human efficacy remain unestablished by the supplied study.
Clinical completion thresholds still require specified sample sizes, follow-up duration, functional targets, comparator adjustments, safety margins and supply targets.
The related-concept distinctions rely on the supplied roster and conceptual descriptions. Detailed records for those other concepts were unavailable.

brief.title: Replacement organs made outside the body
possible: People with a failed organ could receive a replacement built outside the body, large and capable enough to take over its essential work for years. A replacement kidney could free someone from dialysis, the treatment that filters blood when kidneys fail.
why: Manufactured organs could reduce dependence on donated human organs and give more people access to a transplant. For people with kidney failure, a lasting replacement would mean sustained freedom from dialysis.

sources.who: David Y Lo and colleagues at Miromatrix and Mayo Clinic
sources.showed: They removed cells from pig kidneys and added human cells to the remaining tissue framework. The rebuilt kidneys filtered blood outside the body and produced urine after implantation in pigs.
sources.quote: Extending these findings to a clinically relevant model, bioengineered kidneys produce urine with indices of filtration when heterotopically implanted in pigs.
sources.cited_for: Human-sized kidney frameworks can support human cells and aspects of blood filtration.
sources.not_established: They did not establish complete kidney function or lasting replacement in people.

sources.who: Brett D. Anderson, Erek D. Nelson and colleagues
sources.showed: Engineered livers containing human blood-vessel cells and pig liver cells performed several liver functions. They slowed ammonia buildup in pigs with surgically induced liver failure.
sources.quote:
BELs additionally slowed ammonia accumulation during
in vivo perfusion in a porcine model of surgically induced acute liver failure.
sources.cited_for: An engineered liver can perform some of its essential chemical work during blood circulation in an animal.
sources.not_established: The results did not establish lasting replacement of a failed human liver.

sources.showed: They rebuilt rat kidney frameworks with cells. After transplantation into rats, the kidneys received blood from the recipient and produced urine through the urine outlet.
sources.quote: The resulting grafts produced rudimentary urine
sources.cited_for: Rebuilt kidneys can connect to an animal’s circulation and drain urine after implantation.
sources.not_established: The rat results did not establish human-sized organs with enough lasting function to replace failed kidneys.

shown: Miromatrix and Mayo Clinic’s human-sized kidney work reached short animal implants. The final implant test lasted up to five hours. The small study had inconsistent results and lacked cells needed to regulate water, salts and other dissolved substances.
missing: An implanted organ has yet to demonstrate enough lasting function in people to replace a failed organ.
Rebuilt kidneys still need coordinated filtration and control of water, salts and other dissolved substances.
Blood supply, urine drainage and control of immune rejection need to remain effective over time.
Manufacturing must reliably produce organs that meet useful function and safety standards at a practical supply scale.

milestones.label: Implanted organs replace essential function for several years
milestones.explanation: A human study would have to show safe replacement of essential organ function for several years. For kidneys, sustained freedom from dialysis and adequate fluid and salt control would establish useful replacement.

milestones.label: Complications meet agreed safety limits against transplant care
milestones.explanation: Comparisons with appropriate transplants would have to account for recipient and donor differences and meet safety limits agreed beforehand. This would establish whether complications are clinically acceptable.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce outcomes with dependable organ supply
milestones.explanation: Results would have to repeat across manufacturing batches, recipients and independent clinical teams, with documented yield, quality standards, delivery times and capacity. This would establish supply beyond exceptional cases.

milestones.label: Lasting human function has clearly reported requirements and limits
milestones.explanation: Lasting implanted function in people would have to come with clear recipient criteria, immune treatment needs, bodily connections and failure patterns. This would define the conditions under which replacement works.

uncertain: The required study size, duration and functional targets still need clinical justification.
Acceptable complication rates and practical production targets remain to be defined.
Success with one organ would not establish that the same approach works for another.

page.title: Bioengineered solid organs for transplantation
page.definition: A living solid organ built outside the body has enough tissue and functional capacity to replace a failed organ after implantation in a person. Construction includes growing organised tissue or repopulating a decellularized scaffold, the supporting structure left after an organ's cells are removed.

goal.need: The United States kidney waiting list on 30 July 2026 was more than three times the number of kidney transplants performed during 2025. ARPA-H and organ developers pursue biofabrication as an additional source of transplantable organs.

figures.caption: United States organ waiting lists and transplant activity.
figures.note: Waiting lists are snapshots; transplant counts cover a year. HRSA lists kidney–pancreas and heart–lung transplantation separately. These counts do not describe a cohort or a transplant probability.

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, PRINT programme
statements.quote: The platform will use patient-matched organ biofabrication to restore normal human organ function for the kidney, heart, or liver.
Miromatrix is also developing miroliver®, a fully implantable manufactured liver alternative product, and mirokidney®, a fully implantable manufactured kidney alternative product
statements.context: Miromatrix is a United Therapeutics subsidiary.

completion.title: FDA licenses a bioengineered solid organ for implantation to replace failed organ function.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a biologics licence application for a bioengineered solid organ assembled outside the body, with surgical implantation and replacement of failed organ function as its approved use. Nonclinical and clinical evidence establishes safety, purity and potency; manufacturing and facilities meet the applicable requirements. The approved indication determines the required functional benefit and duration. This test is applied separately to each organ.
completion.set_by: United States FDA, 21 CFR 601.2 and 601.20; the general biologics licensing test applied to an implanted organ-replacement indication.
completion.threshold_quote: the manufactured product meets prescribed requirements of safety, purity, and potency
completion.basis: This applies FDA's existing biologics licensing decision to an implanted organ-replacement indication. United Therapeutics identifies biologics licensure as the expected pathway for its recellularized and printed organs. Product-specific clinical evidence and manufacturing controls are assessed together. FDA's licensed cellular-therapy list contains none of the four organ replacements.

milestones.title: A bioengineered organ demonstrates an organ-specific biological function in proof-of-concept testing.
milestones.criterion: An assembled organ demonstrates biological activity in proof-of-concept assays. Examples: kidney, Lo et al., 5 December 2024, five grafts tested across three pig implant sessions, final graft showed filtration indices over 5 hours; liver, Anderson et al., 7 October 2021, three pig recipients observed for 37, 42 and 48 hours with evidence of ammonia metabolism; heart, Ott et al., 13 January 2008, functional measurements in 5/8 rat constructs, about 2% of adult rat-heart function at day 8; lung, Petersen et al., 24 June 2010, gas exchange in four implanted rat lungs for 45–120 minutes. These demonstrate component functions.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, section III.B.4; nonbinding recognition of biological-activity assays as proof-of-concept evidence.
milestones.threshold_quote: in vitro assays intended to assess aspects of the biological activity

milestones.title: Implanted bioengineered organs show function, durability and safety in relevant preclinical models.
milestones.criterion: The intended clinical construct, or a justified comparable product, is tested in biologically relevant animals with controls. Cell/scaffold studies demonstrate biochemical, structural and functional responses, establish dose and duration of effect, and evaluate acute and long-term toxicity, including tumour formation and immune responses. Follow-up is sufficient to show durability for the product and indication. FDA's guidance recommends these results without prescribing a universal animal number or duration.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, sections III.B and IV.E.4–8; nonbinding criteria for cell therapies with implantable scaffolds.
milestones.threshold_quote: but should be sufficient to provide data to show durability of effect.

milestones.title: An IND permitting a clinical study of an implanted bioengineered organ takes effect.
milestones.criterion: An Investigational New Drug (IND) application for a clinical study of an implanted bioengineered organ is in effect: 30 days have elapsed since FDA received it without a clinical hold, or FDA has notified the sponsor that the study may start earlier. Institutional review and informed-consent requirements also apply.
milestones.threshold_quote: Thirty days after FDA receives the IND

milestones.title: A person receives an implanted bioengineered solid organ in a phase 1 clinical investigation.
milestones.criterion: A person receives an implanted bioengineered solid organ in an authorised phase 1 investigation. Adjacent liver evidence: on 26 January 2026, United Therapeutics reported that five patients received external miroliverELAP treatment for at least 44 hours and survived treatment. That press-release result is not peer reviewed and does not establish implantation.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defining initial human introduction; applied here to implantation of the assembled organ.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Controlled human studies provide preliminary evidence that an implanted bioengineered organ works.
milestones.criterion: Controlled clinical studies in intended recipients provide preliminary evidence of effectiveness for organ replacement and identify common short-term adverse effects. FDA describes indication-specific effectiveness and short-term risks as phase 2 study objectives, and preliminary evidence of effectiveness as the condition preceding phase 3. The functional endpoint, effect size and follow-up are specific to the product's clinical protocol.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), describing phase 2 studies and the evidence preceding phase 3; clinical phases may overlap.

milestones.title: Expanded human studies establish the benefit–risk evidence needed to label a bioengineered organ.
milestones.criterion: After preliminary evidence of effectiveness, expanded controlled and uncontrolled human studies establish the additional safety and effectiveness evidence needed to assess the organ's overall benefit–risk relationship and provide an adequate basis for physician labelling for its proposed replacement indication.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(c), describing the conventional phase 3 evidence stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: provide an adequate basis for physician labeling.

not_found: No organ-specific FDA clinical success threshold or common follow-up duration for assembled whole-organ replacement was found.
No registered human implantation study of an assembled whole kidney, heart, liver or lung was located in the ClinicalTrials.gov searches.
The 2026 miroliverELAP conference abstract could not be opened at the journal or in AASLD's abstract PDF.
